questions.question: "If your opponent plays a card, remove a token from this card." The trigger's own event condition names "your opponent". Triggers choose "your opponent" when they resolve (README, MP 4), but here the condition decides whether the trigger happens at all. Who counts?
readings: (A) The trigger fires whenever any opponent plays a card; no choice is offered (the acting player is "your opponent" for that trigger).
(B) The controller picks one opponent when the Morphmajig enters play (RQ-mp-5 lasting text, re-picked if eliminated); only that opponent's plays remove tokens.
(C) The controller picks an opponent each time any opponent plays a card, and the token is removed only if the picked player is the one who played.
questions.recommendation: (A). It is the only reading with no extra choice and no way for the controller to dodge a mandatory drawback; it matches the two-player behavior for every opponent. Sadistic Colonel (same family) should follow the same answer.

questions.question: "While your opponent controls an item and this card is the only member of an attacking party, this card cannot be blocked." RQ-mp-5 says lasting text chooses its opponent when the effect starts applying. For a static gated by a condition that itself names the opponent, when does it "start applying", and is the choice then fixed?
readings: (A) The controller picks one opponent when the card enters play and keeps it until the card leaves or that player is eliminated (then re-picks). Only that opponent's items count, even when another opponent is the one attacked.

(B) The controller picks an opponent each time the condition is checked (each attack/block step), so the condition is met whenever the controller can pick an opponent who controls an item (equivalent to "any opponent controls an item").
(C) The static is gated per defending player: the condition counts only the player being attacked.
questions.recommendation: (A), the literal application of RQ-mp-5. If the user prefers the table-neutral outcome, (B) is the alternative; (C) is not supported by the printed words. Cute Cutpurse clause 0 has the identical text and should follow the same answer.

(B) The player activating is "you" and picks the other player at activation, so any player may use it (collapses to anyPlayer).
(C) The controller and every opponent may use it (RQ-mp-6 extended beyond the one card it was given for).
questions.recommendation: (A): it follows MP 3 and RQ-mp-5 literally, and RQ-mp-6 explicitly says it covers its own card only.

questions.question: "If your opponent plays a tactic, inflict 2 damage to their faction." The trigger condition names "your opponent". Who counts, and when is "your opponent" chosen? (Same family as Guardforce Morphmajig clause 2.)
readings: (A) Any opponent playing a tactic triggers it; "their faction" is that player's faction; no choice is offered.
(B) The controller picks one opponent when the Colonel enters play (RQ-mp-5); only that opponent's tactics trigger it.
(C) The controller picks an opponent each time any opponent plays a tactic, and damage happens only if the picked player is the one who played.
questions.recommendation: (A), consistently with Guardforce Morphmajig: no extra choice, no dodge of a mandatory effect, and per-opponent behavior identical to the two-player collapse.

questions.question: "If you attack, your opponent must pick any number of characters they control. Those characters must block during this battle if they can, and only those characters can block." With several opponents, must the opponent chosen for this block be the player being attacked?
readings: (A) Literal MP 2: the controller picks any opponent. If the pick is not the defending player, that player's characters cannot block (they are not the picker's) so effectively no character can block.
(B) The block implicitly means the defending player: the chosen opponent is forced to be the player being attacked (no choice offered).
questions.recommendation: (A) if "rules decide": MP 2 puts no constraint on the selection, and the same literal rule is applied to every other combat card. (B) is the sensible-looking outcome; the user should decide whether this card deserves the exception.
